data.title: Spinner
data.tagline: A rotating indicator that shows a short, indeterminate wait
data.description: Use a spinner for a brief wait with no reliable completion percentage, such as a submit button, local refresh, or modal task. Name the work in progress; for a long wait, offer cancellation, retry, or a failure result.

distinctions.label: Progress
distinctions.explanation: Spinner only shows that work is still happening; it does not say how much is done. Progress shows overall completion and, when measurable, a percentage.

distinctions.label: Skeleton
distinctions.explanation: Spinner suits a brief local wait. Skeleton reserves the shape of a larger page or content area before it arrives.

avoid: A known file size or completion ratio: use Progress
A predictable full-page layout: use Skeleton
A long wait with no cancel, error, or retry path

lessonPractice.title: Saving usually finishes in two seconds, but remaining work is unknown. What should appear?

options.label: Show a Spinner and Saving in the button, disabling duplicate submission
options.feedback: Correct. A brief wait with unknown completion suits a Spinner and should say what is happening.

options.label: Show Progress slowly moving from 0% to 100%
options.feedback: Without real completion, fake progress misleads people.

options.label: Show no state and update suddenly on success
options.feedback: People cannot tell whether the click worked and may submit again.

data.agentPrompt: When saving starts, show a Spinner and Saving in the current button and disable duplicate clicks; restore it with a visible success or failure result. Simulate a two-second wait and one failure, confirming no duplicate request and both outcomes are visible.

references.title: Progress Indicators Make a Slow System Less Insufferable
